full_judgment:
This Rule, by the preempted, directed against judgment and order dated 9-11-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st court, Narayangonj allowing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 46 of 2003, thereby allowing preemption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on reversing those dated 31-5-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj in Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1994. 

 5. Mr Syed Ridwan Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing for the pre-emptee petitioner, submits that, the depositions of the witnesses and also statement in the petition for pre-emption cannot be given a different meaning by swearing-affidavit before notary public as this affidavit has no value and also that this affidavit cannot be taken into consideration at the appellate stage. 

 7. On consideration of the depositions of the pre-emptor and also opposite party No.1 who stated as: 

 10. I am of the opinion that this finding of reversal by the court of appeal below is not permissible under law. First, to consider affidavit swooned before a notary public is not evidence, nor it is a fact but a certificate of a state of thing. Secondly, such affidavit is to prove, thirdly, concerned notary public is required to be deposed on oath. In absence of these entire legal aspects affidavit sworn before a Notary Public cannot be gone into evidence nor it can be relied. As such Court of appeal below committed illegality in allowing appeal in the petition of pre-emption. I find substance in this Rule.
